text:
The scoreboard said two goals, but the second period said more. UTA out-chanced NJD 1.94 to 0.80 in expected goals over those 20 minutes and turned that edge into three goals, the last of them Lawson Crouse's tip-in at 19:03, a 56 percent look that put UTA up 4-2 and gave the third period a very short runway. NJD had 66 shot attempts to UTA's 63 and 33 shots on goal to 31, yet it trailed on quality all night. Over the full game, UTA's expected goals were 4.26 to NJD's 2.85, and the Utah side won 71 percent of simulated replays.

Special teams tilted it early. Clayton Keller scored on a first-period power play at 1:57, and Nick Schmaltz added another man-advantage goal in the second, so UTA went 2 for 4 while NJD went 1 for 5. Luke Evangelista kept NJD close with two tip-in goals, one on the power play and one at even strength, and Jesper Boqvist cut it to 4-3 at 9:49 of the third. Vincent Trocheck answered at 16:52 with a wrist shot that made it 5-3.

Mikhail Sergachev took first star with three assists, and Schmaltz had a goal and two assists while UTA generated 2.83 expected goals to 0.59 against with him on the ice. Jake Allen allowed five on 31 shots, 0.78 goals worse than expected. Karel Vejmelka stopped 30 of 33 and finished 0.15 below expected, so neither goalie rescued his team. Timo Meier fired eight shots on goal for NJD, but UTA's 21 blocked shots and the second period's lopsided chances kept that pressure from changing the outcome.
